items.title: Armand Hug Interview, 1960-07-14
items.q: my first records were with Shawkey Banana in 1936... And we were playing together then... I was in the band.

ctx.x: No, I didn't record with them at the Owls.

No, my first records were with Shawkey Banana in 1936 when Shawkey Banana came with them. And we were playing together then. Where is the Shawpery? The Shawpery is now called Maison's Beach House out on Ponchacrine Boulevard. Were the records made in New Orleans? Oh, yes. I made the records with Shawkey at the Roosevelt Hotel. Who was in that band anyway? I think it was Ray Bonitas, Augie Chalang, Myer Wine Boyd, and I was in the band.
And then, I was in the band. Where is the Shawpery?

items.title: Armand Hug Interview, 1960-07-14
items.q: Yeah, Sharky was playing. We had Sharky. I think Leo Brookhoven was playing Fitch trumpet. Sharky was playing second trumpet.

ctx.x: Some of them even have the same name. Exactly, you know. Yeah. Different instrument.

Yeah, that's right. We had a good little band at the original 25 Club. That was back off the Pontchartrain Road where the Honeysuckle Inn was. You may have heard of the Honeysuckle Inn. The Honeysuckle Inn and the original 25 Club were right across from each other. Is that? Sharky opened at the original 25 Club and then left there and went across the street to the Honeysuckle Inn. And I was playing over at the original 25 Club with Eddie Miller and Bill Padron. And I think Sharky was playing over at the other, at…
There's a place, I think one day I was at the market with Bob Coquille, do you remember that? It was about the original 2 Bits Club, is that the same thing?

items.title: Armand Hug Interview, 1960-07-14
items.q: Like Shawty used to stop in.

ctx.x: Back to the piano players, are there any others that you remember in that era that were outstanding?

Well, I would say that after I began playing around the suburban movie houses in town, I used to play for silent movies in those days. Played with three pieces. We used to get a dollar a piece a night. We didn't even get our call fair, but I was playing with a violin player by the name of Grasshoff and a drummer, Surpass I believe was his name. We used to go down to the St. Maurice Avenue Theater and play for these silent movies. The silent movies got a bad deal in those days because we were playing Tiger Rag or…
Would he sit down at the piano?
